summary: This paper demonstrates that repetition-code quantum error correction (QEC) can substantially enhance axion dark matter search sensitivity in CMOS semiconductor spin qubit arrays by mitigating longitudinal dephasing that otherwise suppresses entanglement gain. Integrating repetition codes with logical GHZ block entanglement yields closed-form quantum Fisher information expressions showing that modest QEC cycle frequencies restore multi-qubit sensing advantages across a broad axion mass range.
motivation: Semiconductor spin qubit platforms searching for axion-electron coupling via entangled GHZ states suffer from strong local longitudinal dephasing ($T_2^* \sim 100$ µs in current devices with $T_{2,1/f} \sim 200$ µs), which rapidly suppresses the $\sqrt{N_\mathrm{phys}}$ sensitivity gain and makes unencoded entanglement compete only with the standard quantum limit.
method: The authors combine a phase-flip repetition code (encoding each logical qubit in $n_\mathrm{rep}$ physical spins) with logical GHZ states of size $k_L$, deriving the effective logical dephasing rate $\gamma_\mathrm{eff}(n_\mathrm{rep})$ that replaces the physical rate $\gamma_\mathrm{loc}$, and optimizing the quantum Fisher information by balancing signal amplification against dephasing of the entangled state at each axion mass.
result: With realistic Si/SiGe CMOS parameters ($p_g, p_m \sim 10^{-4}$, $\tau_\mathrm{cyc} = 2$ µs, $T_{2,M} = 2$ ms), an optimized configuration $(n_\mathrm{rep}, k_L) = (13, 14)$ achieves a Fisher information gain $\eta_\mathrm{seg} \approx 11.1$ relative to the SQL benchmark, yielding approximately order-of-magnitude improvement in projected sensitivity to $g_{ae}$ across the mass range $10^{-6}$–$10^{-3}$ eV where $T_\mathrm{seg}$ is hardware-limited.
